source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
A small moth in the genus Prays (ដង្កូវសំបកគ្រូច, family Yponomeutidae) has larvae that bore into the rind/peel of citrus fruit - the source notes this pest is a particular problem on thick-skinned fruit such as pomelo. The larva tunnels into the fruit peel and the flesh just beneath it, and the entry wound frequently lets in rot organisms, causing the fruit to spoil or drop before harvest.

Because the larva feeds hidden inside the fruit for much of its development, damage is often noticed only once a small entry hole and surrounding rot become visible on the fruit surface, by which point internal damage is already done.

Control relies on monitoring fruit during the vulnerable early development period, prompt removal and destruction of infested and fallen fruit to break the pest's life cycle, and orchard sanitation generally, since fallen infested fruit left on the ground can allow the pest to complete its life cycle and reinfest the next fruiting flush.
